object_readings.reading: Unnamed motorway ramps west of the station on a bridge structure; a walking barrier except where streets pass under it.
US 1 and SR 970 ramps on bridges to the west; they separate the waterfront core from the blocks beyond.
A short piece of the Downtown Distributor at the edge of the disc; marginal for this station.
Other railroad trackage far to the north-west, outside the quarter mile; little effect on access to this station.
The existing Metromover guideway passes the reference point; it is the asset the study converts.
The largest zoning polygon is an Urban Core transect that contains the reference point: dense development is permitted here, which is consistent with a workplace core but does not prove activity.
A Civic Space zone east of the station signals park and event activity that the commute-based scenarios do not contain.
Coastal water is the largest land-use class in the disc; about a third of the half-mile disc cannot hold origins or destinations.
Municipal parks are a visible share of the disc: a visitor destination, not a commute one.
A vacant commercial parcel close to the reference point with a lot far larger than the smallest platform module.
A very large municipal parcel next to the station, consistent with the waterfront park.

patterns.statement: Water to the east and motorway ramps to the west leave a north-south band of urban core land as the station's effective surroundings.
The guideway loops through the disc while other railroad trackage stays at its north-west edge.

candidate_sites.why: Vacant commercial land within the inner band, with a lot many times the smallest module footprint.
caveats: ownership, access, structure and approvals unknown
a vacant classification is a tax record, not a site survey

data_anomalies.statement: Reference folios appear as parcels with a lot size of zero; they are condominium master records and should not be read as land.

not_determinable: Whether the motorway ramps can be crossed on foot near the station: no walk model and no crossing data.
What the intensity letter in the zone names permits: the legend does not define it.
